Full Comments:
Spoke with Rob regarding the situation where an application was completed, marked as delivered, and used to obtain funding so parts could be ordered before the repairs were completed. He explained that this involved a specific customer who wanted to secure approval but keep the vehicle until the required parts arrived. Because he could not release the vehicle without ordering the parts, he marked the deal as delivered to receive funding.

I reminded Rob that this is not the correct process. The proper procedure is to obtain approval, complete all repairs on the vehicle, and only then mark the application as delivered once the work has been completed. Applications should not be marked as delivered at any point prior to the completion of repairs. Rob acknowledged the issue and stated that he will not do this again moving forward.

Full Comments:
We should not enroll a merchant who runs a shop out of his house, especially a discretionary product such as car stereo and tint. EP is used to facilitate financing for traditional brick-and-mortar businesses. 

Additionally, it seems that the city of Los Angeles does not permit any type of an auto maintenance or repair shop to be operated out of a personal residence. 

Licensing for a physical location is a governed by the local government and not by the state, so even if an ITIN, seller's permit and business bank account were issued for this business, these licensing boards do not regulate the physical location of a business. 

We need to pass on this one.
